name: hidden-and-archived
why: Archived repos appear in no signal: a tombstone's open issues are noise by definition, whether the position says so itself or the caller passes the repo in as already gone. A foundry-hidden mark is a different thing and takes a different treatment - the row stays in the queue carrying its mark, so a reader can hold it back and still say how many it is holding. Dropping it outright would make a deliberate choice look like a loss. The mark has two scopes and they must not be confused: the LABEL hides one ticket, so its repo's other rows are untouched; the TOPIC hides a whole repo, so EVERY signal it raises is marked - red CI and unreleased commits included, not its tickets alone. A reader that carried the topic to the issue rows alone would leave a repo it was told to hide still shouting about its red default branch.
